name: Selina-4,7(11)-diene

papers.title: Chemical composition and in vitro antimicrobial activities of the essential oils from endemic Psiadia species growing in mauritius

evidence: Measured in 5 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.35–3.76% of total volatiles (0.07–0.75mg per chew).

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selina-4,7(11)-diene is a sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule often found in the essential oils of certain plants. As a volatile compound, it contributes to the complex botanical scents of the herbs it inhabits. People most likely encounter it when smelling or consuming traditional herbal preparations.
consumer_summary.found_in: Based on research literature, it has been identified in the essential oils of Valeriana tangutica (a species of valerian) and in endemic Psiadia shrubs native to Mauritius.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to Selina-4,7(11)-diene for its potential role in botanical defense systems. They are exploring how essential oils containing this sesquiterpene interact with various bacteria and fungi, including challenging strains like Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational research (Oxford level 2b) alongside laboratory microbial sensitivity tests.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward Selina-4,7(11)-diene having properties that may support a healthy microbial balance.
structure_function.basis: This rests on two papers, including human observational data and in vitro microbial sensitivity tests.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether this molecule, as part of botanical essential oils, can directly inhibit the growth of problematic bacteria and fungi. If this bears out, it could help explain the traditional use of the plants that contain it and inspire new botanical defense strategies.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human trial (Oxford level 1b) applying a standardized topical formulation of Selina-4,7(11)-diene to measure its effect on skin flora and specific bacterial colonization over a two-week period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) alongside laboratory studies evaluating its antimicrobial potential.
